what: The player's default model becomes z-ai/glm-5.3-flash, asked by json_object pinned to Z.AI under its own request name while every other model keeps json-schema-retry byte-identical, with OpenRouter's reported provider recorded on every model call through score and compare, an atomic run-directory claim, run.json's world recorded relative to the repository root, and GLM and Haiku re-scored and compared on copies of the four goal sets under corpus/experiments/glm-default/.
why: rudy decided on 2026-11-01 to switch the default to GLM-5.3-flash pinned to Z.AI, which reached 137 of 141 at Haiku's cost per run, and the harness could neither send that request nor show who served a call; design: docs/work/glm-default/design.md.
stakes: With no model named, the target and the words are asked of z-ai/glm-5.3-flash by json_object with provider order [z-ai] and allow_fallbacks false, under the request name json-object-z-ai-retry, recorded in run.json and the score.
Every model not listed in the request table, anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5 included, is sent a body whose JSON text equals today's json-schema-retry body, under the name json-schema-retry.

Every model call in a new run.json records the provider OpenRouter reported for it, or null when it reported none; each score entry and file counts model calls per provider, and the compare shows providers per set and per moved goal.
compare reads each side under its own model's request, refuses a score whose request is not its model's, and writes to a name carrying both requests, never a committed compare file's name.
A run directory is claimed by the mkdir that creates it, retried on EEXIST, so concurrent score processes each get their own and none fails.
run.json records world relative to the repository root, and no new run.json carries an absolute path; committed runs are left as they are, and #8 closes with this work order.
A score with no model named lands on the default's named path; no score or compare writes any file under corpus/goals, and C9 still reads the committed calibration.score.json.

GLM (no --model) and Haiku are each scored once per set on byte-identical copies of the four goal files under corpus/experiments/glm-default/ and compared there, a test pins each copy's sha256 to its original, an unanswered target halts for a ruling, and spend past $0.50 stops for the orchestrator.
The prompts, the parse and the one identical retry are unchanged; the harness still imports nothing from the engine or the server.

criteria.given: a hosted bench in a real browser, a Jev stand-in and a chat completions stand-in that keeps every request body
criteria.when: tests/player.test.ts runs the run command as the operator does, once with no --model, once with --model anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5 and once with --model openai/gpt-test (a model the request table does not list)
criteria.then: the run with no --model fails if any target or words body differs from arm F's: it posts model z-ai/glm-5.3-flash with exactly {model, messages, response_format: {type: json_object}, provider: {order: ["z-ai"], allow_fallbacks: false}, usage: {include: true}} and no other key, and records wordsModel z-ai/glm-5.3-flash and request json-object-z-ai-retry. The Haiku run's bodies, as JSON text, equal today's json-schema-retry bodies (response_format json_schema strict with name target or words and wireSchema of the schema, provider {require_parameters: true}, usage include, keys in today's order), and it records request json-schema-retry. The unlisted model gets the json-schema-retry body and name. Each request name is asserted beside its body

mutations.change: add require_parameters: true to the GLM body in harness/src/words.ts
swap the order of provider and usage in the json-schema-retry body
make requestFor() return JSON_OBJECT_Z_AI for every model

criteria.given: a chat completions stand-in whose target answer body carries provider "Z.AI" and whose words answer body carries no provider, and a Jev stand-in
criteria.when: tests/player.test.ts runs the run command and reads run.json
criteria.then: run.json is wrong if a model call lacks a provider key or a Jev call has one: the target call records provider "Z.AI", the words call records provider null, and no Jev call has a provider key; a refused attempt and its retry each record their own body's provider

mutations.change: leave provider out of the Call recordAttempts() records in harness/src/run.ts
read provider from body.model instead of body.provider in attempt()

criteria.given: a temp goal set named named of two goals, a pre-written named.score.json holding known bytes, model stand-ins reporting providers, and a Jev stand-in
criteria.when: tests/score.test.ts runs the score command with no --model, then with --model anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5
criteria.then: the scores are wrong if named.score.json changes by a byte: the no-model score writes named.z-ai_glm-5.3-flash.json-object-z-ai-retry.score.json with model z-ai/glm-5.3-flash and request json-object-z-ai-retry, scorePath(goals, "named", undefined) returns that path, and the Haiku score writes named.anthropic_claude-haiku-5.5.json-schema-retry.score.json; each goal entry's providers counts its run's model calls per provider in first-seen order and the file's providers sums them

mutations.change: make scorePath() return <set>.score.json when model is undefined
count Jev calls into a goal's providers in harness/src/score.ts

criteria.given: in a temp directory, score files written by this code for z-ai/glm-5.3-flash under json-object-z-ai-retry and anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5 under json-schema-retry with their run.json files, one goal Haiku held and GLM lost whose GLM score entry's providers differ from what its run.json's calls would count, a pre-existing <candidate>.vs.<baseline>.json-schema-retry.compare.json and .md holding known bytes, a Haiku score file made before providers existed; and in a second directory a GLM score file at its path whose request is json-schema-retry
criteria.when: tests/compare.test.ts runs the compare command over each directory
criteria.then: over the first it writes z-ai_glm-5.3-flash.json-object-z-ai-retry.vs.anthropic_claude-haiku-5.5.json-schema-retry.compare.json and .md, leaves the pre-existing compare files byte-identical, records requests {baseline: json-schema-retry, candidate: json-object-z-ai-retry}, renders a providers column per set (not recorded for the pre-provider score), and shows the lost goal's providers as its score entries record them. Over the second it exits 1 naming the score file, the request found and the one expected, writing nothing

mutations.change: check both sides in readScore() against the candidate's request
count a moved goal's providers from its run.json in compare.ts instead of taking its score entry's

criteria.given: one empty corpus directory and a fixed startedAt
criteria.when: a test starts several child bun processes at once, each calling claimRunDir() from harness/src/run.ts many times for that corpus and startedAt
criteria.then: the claim is broken if any process throws or two claims return one directory: every process exits 0, every returned runDir exists, and the number of distinct directories equals the number of claims

mutations.change: restore the existsSync check before a separate mkdirSync in claimRunDir()
take any mkdir error as already claimed instead of only code EEXIST: a test that claimRunDir rethrows an error other than EEXIST goes red

criteria.given: a run of the run command over the default world with the stand-ins, from the checkout
criteria.then: run.json leaks a path if any string value anywhere in it is one path.isAbsolute accepts: parameters.world is "world" and no string value in the record is absolute

mutations.change: record world as options.worldDir in parametersOf() in harness/src/run.ts

criteria.then: a copy has drifted if its sha256 differs from its corpus/goals original: a test asserts each of the four copies' sha256 equals the original's

criteria.given: the job's branch after the live comparison is committed
criteria.when: git diff main -- corpus/goals and the gate's tests run
criteria.then: a committed record was written over if the diff is not empty: git diff main -- corpus/goals prints nothing, C9 (tests/rule.test.ts) passes reading corpus/goals/calibration.score.json unchanged, and the harness boundary test passes, the harness importing nothing from the engine or the server

criteria.given: the built code in the job's worktree, the real OpenRouter and Jev endpoints, the registered thresholds, and the four copies in corpus/experiments/glm-default
criteria.when: the builder runs bun run score --goals corpus/experiments/glm-default/calibration.json --sweep --tick-minutes 10 with no --model, the same for blind-1, blind-2-spent and blind-2 without --sweep, then the four with --model anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5, then bun run compare --baseline anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5 --candidate z-ai/glm-5.3-flash --goals with the four copies
criteria.then: the comparison failed if any target is unanswered (that halts to the orchestrator and is never counted or re-run without its ruling) or the summed costUsd of the eight scores passes 0.50 USD (that stops for the orchestrator): eight score files and the two compare files are written in corpus/experiments/glm-default, 94 runs land in corpus/runs, every GLM run records wordsModel z-ai/glm-5.3-flash and request json-object-z-ai-retry with every model call's provider Z.AI, every Haiku run records request json-schema-retry with a provider on every model call, every run's parameters.world is world, and the lane result reports each model's reached, retries, providers and cost per set, and the losses and gains

walks.when: after merge, on main, with no endpoint called: bun run compare --baseline anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5 --candidate z-ai/glm-5.3-flash --goals corpus/experiments/glm-default/calibration.json --goals corpus/experiments/glm-default/blind-1.json --goals corpus/experiments/glm-default/blind-2-spent.json --goals corpus/experiments/glm-default/blind-2.json
walks.then: it exits 0 and rewrites the two compare files in corpus/experiments/glm-default with git diff showing no change to either, and corpus/goals is untouched

outOfScope.summary: allow_fallbacks false means a Z.AI outage or refusal stops every default run with a status refusal instead of routing GLM to another provider.

frequency.records: corpus/experiments/glm-request/F/calls.jsonl, arm F's model calls pinned to Z.AI with no fallback, those not answered 200

outOfScope.summary: Z.AI has no structured_outputs, so GLM's request asks for any JSON object and relies on the prompt for the shape, with zod and the one retry as the only check of it.

frequency.records: corpus/experiments/glm-request/analysis.json, arm F's runs lost to a schema failure

outOfScope.summary: The plain <set>.score.json files are never written again, so the calibration record C9 reads can no longer be refreshed by a model-less score; a new calibration (#6) must name its own writer.

frequency.records: git ls-files corpus/goals/*.score.json, the committed plain score files

outOfScope.summary: The new compare cannot regenerate the committed json-schema-retry or pre-request compare reports, whose names carry one request or none; they stay committed as they are.

frequency.records: git ls-files corpus/goals/*.compare.*, the committed compare files

outOfScope.summary: Score files made before providers were recorded show `not recorded` in the compare's providers column.

frequency.records: git ls-files corpus/goals/*.score.json, committed score files without providers

outOfScope.summary: A world outside the repository is recorded as a relative path climbing out of it, which names directories above the checkout.

frequency.records: corpus/runs/*/run.json, committed runs whose world is not the world folder at a checkout's root

outOfScope.summary: The experiment folder holds copies of the four goal files, kept equal to corpus/goals only by the sha256 test.

frequency.reason: The four copies are pinned to their corpus/goals originals by a sha256 test the gate runs, so a drifted copy cannot pass the gate and never reaches a score.

outOfScope.summary: The request table is keyed by exact model id, so another GLM id, a later version included, is asked by json-schema-retry until it is listed.
